traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 85 Thymelaeaceae: trees or shrubs, rarely herbs; leaves opposite or alternate, mostly small; no stipules; flowers often in bracted heads, spikes or racemes, rarely alone, bisexual or of one sex, regular or slightly irregular; calyx a tube, sometimes petal-like, its lobes 4 or 5 (read as a hypanthium crowned by the lobes); petals scale-like or none; ovary superior; fruit staying shut (drupes and nuts in Daphne and kin), left unstated. Head-like clusters from 'terminal bracteate heads' (the OCR is broken there; inferred).

traits.leaf_division.note: APweb, Malvales page, Thymelaeaceae (read 2026-10-16): leaves entire, no stipules.

traits.perianth.note: Wikipedia, Thymelaeaceae (read 2026-10-16): sepals, petals and staminodes hard to tell apart; the showy parts are the petal-like calyx lobes on the tube. APweb mentions a corolla in some. Weighting inferred.

traits.corolla_shape.note: APweb, Malvales page, Thymelaeaceae (read 2026-10-16): long hypanthium tube with lobes spreading at its mouth (Daphne-like flower): a narrow tube with a flat limb.

traits.stamens.note: APweb, Malvales page, Thymelaeaceae (read 2026-10-16): stamens 2-5 or 10, up to 80 in Gonystyloideae. Wikipedia (read 2026-10-16): once or twice the calyx lobes, 1-2 in Pimelea. Typical 8 (twice four lobes) inferred.

traits.carpels.note: APweb, Malvales page, Thymelaeaceae (read 2026-10-16): carpels 2-5, often 2 with one locule not developing.

traits.fruit_type.note: APweb, Malvales page, Thymelaeaceae (read 2026-10-16): capsule, drupe or achene-like. Wikipedia (read 2026-10-16): fruit olive-like. 'usually' drupe inferred.

traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Thymelaeaceae (read 2026-10-17): lamina undivided. Wikipedia, Daphne: undivided leaves.
